system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}
prompt:
Trial: SPARCL NCT00147602 - Lipitor In The Prevention Of Stroke, For Patients Who Have Had A Previous Stroke
Investigational drug: atorvastatin
Document: Short-term adjuvant atorvastatin improves frequency domain indices of heart rate variability in stable systolic heart failure (journal, published 2005-05-01, source pmid:16142595)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
Short-term adjuvant atorvastatin improves frequency domain indices of heart rate variability in stable systolic heart failure

UNLABELLED: The autonomic nervous system marks beneficial drug responses in systolic heart failure management. The impact of statin therapy in this broad disease class is unclear and patient studies are extremely limited. METHODS: We studied a group of 23 patients with stable systolic ventricular impairment and randomised them single (patient) blind to high dose Atorvastatin 40 mg daily or placebo in addition to standard therapies over a 12-week treatment interval. Impact on the autonomic nervous system was assessed by anonymised short-term (20 min) standardised supine heart rate variability analyses. RESULTS: Two subjects withdrew one due to decompensation and one due to gastric intolerance. The remaining subjects completed both monitoring events without changes in standard medicines. Frequency domain but not time domain HRV indices improved with active statin therapy suggesting beneficial effects in attenuating sympathetic tone. CONCLUSIONS: In this small study we saw short-term high potency statin treatment had a beneficial impact on frequency domain HRV measures suggestive of an impact on sympatho-activation. We found no effect on time domain HRV indices. This may suggest a lesser or no effect on parasympathetic tone.
--- END ---
